groups.title: Loader Fundamentals
groups.question: Your Remix loader returns a database model with dates and methods, and the page receives something different. Explain what a loader must return.

followUps.The loader Function Contract: What does a loader receive and what can it return?
followUps.json() Helper and Response Objects: What does a Response helper like json() give you?

evidence.text: A loader receives the request, params and context.
It returns a Response or data that can be serialised.
Class instances, functions or circular data do not survive the trip to the browser.
It creates a Response with the right content type.
It lets you set status codes and headers like caching.
Returning a Response gives full control over the HTTP reply.

groups.title: Parallel and Dependent Loading
groups.question: Your dashboard's nested routes each need data, and one slow widget delays the whole page. Explain how Remix loads data across routes.

followUps.Parallel Loaders Across Nested Routes: How does Remix run loaders for nested routes?
followUps.Deferred Data with defer() and Await: How can a loader let the page render before slow data is ready?

evidence.text: Remix runs all matching route loaders at the same time.
This avoids waiting for parent data before child data loads.
Shared data like the user session belongs in a parent loader.

notEnough: Only saying loaders run in parallel.

evidence.text: A loader can return slow data as an unresolved promise.
The page renders immediately with the fast data.
The Await component shows the slow part when it arrives, with a fallback meanwhile.

notEnough: Only saying data can be deferred.

groups.title: Type-Safe Data Loading
groups.question: Your component's loader types drift from what the loader actually returns, and every request hits the origin even for public data. Explain typing and caching loader data.

followUps.Typing useLoaderData with TypeOf: How does useLoaderData<typeof loader> keep types in sync?
followUps.Loader Caching and HTTP Cache Headers: How can loader responses be cached by a CDN?

evidence.text: Passing typeof loader infers the component's data type from the loader.
There is no separate type to keep in sync.
The inferred type reflects the serialised data the page receives.

notEnough: Only saying it types the data.

evidence.text: Loaders can set Cache-Control headers on their Response.
A CDN can then serve cached copies close to users.
Personalised data must not be cached publicly.

groups.title: Request and URL Access
groups.question: Your search loader parses the query string with regex, and protected pages briefly render before kicking users out. Explain how loaders should read requests and guard routes.

followUps.Accessing request.url and URLSearchParam: How should a loader read query parameters?
followUps.throw redirect() for Authorization Guard: Why throw redirect() from a loader to protect a route?

evidence.text: Loaders receive the full Request, including URL, headers and cookies.
new URL(request.url) and searchParams read query values reliably.
Manual string parsing breaks on encoding and edge cases.

notEnough: Only saying you read the URL.

evidence.text: Throwing redirect stops the loader immediately.
The redirect happens on the server before any page renders.
Protected data and markup never reach users who are not allowed.
